hazards.finding: Baal is Reaiah son at5:5; Beerah and exile disclosed at5:6, not5:5.
The son-of chain is backward through ancestors. Chief role applies carefully to the named syntactic subject, not every ancestor.
Jetur/Naphish/Nodab are collective enemies; do not force ancestor or place identity. Captivity and destinations appear26, not initial names at19/23/24.
The first priest genealogy says became father of; the singer genealogies say son of. Their direction differs and must not be template-copied.
Repeated Ahitub/Zadok/Amariah/Azariah occur at different generations. Match exact parents and avoid next-verse children in initial fields.
Repeated Elkanah/Assir appear in multiple genealogy positions; same spelling does not settle identity.
Song-service introduction precedes Heman/Asaph; an introductory musical-service role can be supported by prior context. Asaph ancestry to Levi continues through43.
Territory clauses carry over city rows. Hukok6:75 follows Asher6:74; Naphtali begins6:76. Kedesh6:72 Issachar differs from Kedesh in Galilee6:76. Do not infer a modern coordinate from shared name.
